title: The globular cluster NGC 3201
caption: The globular cluster NGC 3201, imaged by the MPG/ESO 2.2-meter telescope

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: This color composite shows the globular cluster NGC 3201, captured with the Wide Field Imager on the MPG/ESO 2.2-meter telescope at La Silla. It lies about 16 000 light-years away, toward the southern constellation of Vela.

Globular clusters are large, densely packed swarms of stars, some containing up to millions of members. They are among the oldest objects astronomers observe, and are presumed to be roughly as old as the Milky Way itself, dating from the early period after the Big Bang. That makes them valuable records of our galaxy's distant past.

The data were collected for the ESO Imaging Survey, a public survey run by ESO and its member states to prepare for first light of the Very Large Telescope. First light is the moment a new telescope begins observing.

understand.summary: The Wide Field Imager on the MPG/ESO 2.2-meter telescope imaged the cluster through blue, visual and near-infrared filters. The source does not publish which color was assigned to each filter.
understand.eye: Part of the data is near-infrared light, which the eye cannot see, and the long exposures gather far more light than any eye.

explore: The original image and data were released through the survey's Pre-Flames data pages. The caption gives a distance of about 16 000 light-years, while catalog data lists about 15,000.
